findings.reason: either the default margin or the missing 15 s / 97% bounds must move, and a node that builds to the stated numbers passes the live instrument and fails the plan's own record.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires the default margin 1.5 to deliver at least 97% of the simulated plateau with a 90th-percentile gate wait under 15 s on both workloads, but §2's own table (line 63, "Offered load × 1.5", 444 tok/s at 8.9/16.3 s) and `docs/evidence/fragments/the-local-lane-delivers-its-plateau/sim-offered-w12.log` (x1.5 row: tok/s 444, wait p90 16.3 s) record 16.3 s p90 on the whole-night workload, and 444 tok/s is 92.4% to 95.4% of every plateau figure the plan itself states (§1 "about 470", `s6.html` 480.7 fed / 465.3 starved); the arm therefore fails at the margin the same unit just fixed as the default, so the node's gate cannot pass as written

findings.reason: the default margin is the unit's central decision, and a basis that cannot be re-run leaves the decision resting on a number a reader cannot check.
findings.text: §4 justifies the new default with "in the §3 simulation a margin of 1.25 leaves the starved workload at 95.9% to 98.9% of its plateau across three seeds", but the committed evidence has no margin-1.25 case for the offered-load rule (`sim-offered-w12.log` and `late-offered.log` carry x1.0, x1.1, x1.2, x1.3, x1.5 only) and `imas_ambix/agent/lane_sim.py` exposes no margin control at all, so the figure is presented as a measurement with nothing behind it, while the nearest grid points read differently (x1.2 → 84% of time at width, x1.3 → 92.8% on the whole-night workload)
